{{< pagebreak >}}

Disciplines are the signature mechanic of *Heroes of Legend.* They're how the game knows what your hero has mastered. Not just skills, *domains of power.* Fire. Blades. Protection. The forces and forms your character has attuned to through training, study, or sheer stubborn repetition.

Here's the important part: **Disciplines are prerequisites, not rolls.** You don't roll your Fire Discipline. You don't add your Blades Discipline to an attack. Disciplines are the gate, you need them to *unlock* skills, abilities, and talents. Once you've got them, they represent permanent mastery. No expiration. No forgetting.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## What Are Disciplines?

A Discipline represents a domain of expertise or power your hero has internalized. It's the difference between "I picked up a sword once" and "I've trained with blades for ten years." Between "I read a book about fire" and "Fire answers when I call."

**Example:** A warrior with 3 Blade Disciplines has spent years mastering swords, every angle, every grip, every weakness in every guard. A mage with 3 Fire Disciplines doesn't just cast flames, they *understand* flame, the way a shipwright understands wood. A ranger with 2 Animal Disciplines has bonded with the wild in ways city-folk will never comprehend.

You don't roll Disciplines. You *collect* them. They're permanent markers on your character sheet that say: "I've earned this."

{{< pagebreak >}}

## The Discipline Taxonomy

| Category | Discipline | Represents |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| **Elemental** | **Fire** | Flame, heat, passion, destruction |
| | **Earth** | Stone, stability, endurance, crafting |
| | **Wind** | Air, speed, storms, precision |
| | **Water** | Ice, flow, healing, adaptation |
| **Weapon** | **Blades** | Swords, daggers, finesse and precision |
| | **Axes** | Axes, cleavers, brutal chopping power |
| | **Polearms** | Spears, halberds, reach and control |
| | **Archery** | Bows, crossbows, ranged precision |
| | **Heavy Weapon** | Greatswords, greataxes, mauls, two-handed power |
| | **Unarmed** | Fists, gauntlets, grappling, close-quarters combat |
| **Defense** | **Protection** | Shields, warding, guarding allies |
| | **Armor** | Heavy armor proficiency, damage soaking |
| **Primal** | **Animal** | Beasts, nature, shapeshifting, instinct |
| | **Plants** | Flora, growth, thorns, verdant magic |
| **Arcane** | **Energy** | Raw magical force, metamagic, spellcraft |
| **Divine** | **Life** | Healing, vitality, living things |
| | **Religion** | Faith, blessings, holy power |
| **Esoteric** | **Mind** | Psionics, illusions, mental influence |
| | **Summon** | Calling, binding, conjuring creatures |

Nineteen Disciplines. Seven categories. Your hero's path through them defines everything they can do.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Acquiring Disciplines

### Starting Disciplines

Your starting Disciplines come from your ancestry (1), your culture (2), and your class (see the Class Disciplines table below). General Disciplines are wildcards earned through talents and progression; they can substitute for any specific Discipline at the Novice tier. Need 1 Fire for a Firebolt? A General Discipline covers it. Need 2 Fire for a Fireball? That's Adept, you need the real thing. General Disciplines get you started, but they won't carry you to mastery.

### Class Disciplines

Your class hands you specific Disciplines at creation. These are your foundation, what your training, tradition, or sheer talent has already taught you:

| Class | Starting Disciplines |
|-------|---------------------|
| Protector | 2 Armor, 2 Protection |
| Blade | 3 Blades |
| Arcanist | 2 Fire, 1 Energy, 1 Wind (or any 4 elemental) |
| Shepherd | 2 Protection, 2 Animal |
| Intellect | 3 of any type (flexible) |
| Odd | 3 of any type, must be from different categories |
| Leader | 2 Protection, 1 Energy, 1 any |
| Unbalanced | 2 of one type, 2 of its opposite (Fire/Water or Earth/Wind) |
| Shadow | 2 Blades, 1 Mind |

### Progression

At levels 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18, you gain one additional Discipline of your choice. Class-favored Disciplines, the ones your class gave you at creation, are always available. Cross-class Disciplines may require narrative justification or story events. Want your Blade to pick up Fire? Make it a story. Find a mentor. Touch a primordial flame. Earn it.

### Magic Items

Rare magic items may grant temporary or permanent Disciplines while attuned or wielded. A *Sword of the Phoenix* might grant +1 Fire Discipline in your hands. Set it down, lose the power. These items are treasures, and the DA should make you work for them.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Disciplines as Prerequisites

Skills, abilities, and talents require specific Disciplines before you can learn them. No Disciplines, no purchase. It's that simple.

| Skill/Ability | Disciplines Required | Tier |
|--------------|---------------------|------|
| Longsword | 1 Blade, 1 Heavy Weapon | Adept |
| Dagger | 1 Blade | Novice |
| Greataxe | 1 Axe, 2 Heavy Weapons | Adept |
| Fireball | 2 Fire + 1 Energy | Adept |
| Volcanic Eruption | 3 Fire + 1 Earth | Master |
| Chain Mail | 2 Armor | Novice |
| Shield Block | 1 Protection | Novice |
| Animal Companion | 2 Animal | Adept |
| Magic Missile | 1 Energy | Novice |
| Counterspell | 2 Energy + 1 Reason | Adept |

### General Disciplines Substitution

General Disciplines substitute for specific Disciplines at Novice tier only (1:1). General Disciplines cannot substitute at the Adept or Master tier.

Need 1 Fire for Firebolt? A General covers it. Need 2 Fire for Fireball at Adept? You need the real thing, no substitutions. Need 3 Fire and 1 Earth for Volcanic Eruption? You need every one of those Disciplines the hard way. General gets you in the door. Beyond that, you walk through on your own.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## The Discipline Ladder

Every ability, skill, and spell follows a three-tier ladder. The higher you climb, the more Disciplines you need, the bigger the payoff.

| Tier | DP Cost (any class) | Discipline Requirement | Level Gate | General Subs OK? |
|------|---------------------|------------------------|------------|-------------------|
| **Novice** | 1 DP | 1 specific Discipline | None (Level 1) | Yes (1:1) |
| **Adept** | 2 DP | 2 Disciplines (may differ in type) | Level 3 | No |
| **Master** | 3-4 DP | 3-4 Disciplines across 2+ types (no single type > 3) | Level 7 | No |

**Novice** is your foundation. One Discipline, one DP, you're in the door. Any class can buy any Novice ability at 1 DP regardless of their favored costs (see @sec-chapter-classes). General Disciplines can stand in for specific ones at this tier, a General covers 1 Fire for Firebolt.

**Adept** requires two Disciplines. They might be two ranks of the same type (2 Fire for Flame Strike) or two different types (2 Fire + 1 Energy for Fireball, 2 Water + 1 Wind for Ice Storm). The point is depth: you've moved past dabbling into real investment. Level 3 is the gate; you've earned enough field experience to handle the real power.

**Master** demands three to four Disciplines across at least two types, and no single type can count for more than 3. A spell requiring 3 Fire + 1 Earth is Master. One requiring 4 Fire alone is not, there's no such thing as a one-trick Master. The ladder enforces breadth at the top. Level 7 is the gate. By the time you're casting Master spells, you've been through enough to know when *not* to use them.

**General Disciplines** are your wildcards. They substitute 1:1 for specific Disciplines at Novice tier only. Two Generals don't make an Adept. Three Generals don't make a Master. Generals get you started and can fill in odd gaps in the mid-game, but the upper tiers require the real thing, earned through class training, progression, or story events. See "General Disciplines Substitution" below.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Damage Budget {#sec-damage-budget}

Every damaging spell, ability, and maneuver in *Heroes of Legend* is built on a single table. This is the balance spine. Spells are the guide; everything else keys off them.

| Tier | Discipline Requirement | Damage (Weak / Standard / Strong) |
|------|------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Novice** | 1 Discipline | 2 / 4 / 6 |
| **Adept** | 2 Disciplines | 6 / 9 / 12 |
| **Master** | 3-4 Disciplines | 9 / 15 / 21 |

::: {.callout-note}
## How to Read the Budget

The numbers are damage dice rolled on a hit, always-hit means the question is never *if*, only *how hard*. A Novice Firebolt deals 2d6 on a Weak result, 4d6 on Standard, 6d6 on Strong. An Adept Fireball deals 6d6/9d6/12d6. A Master Volcanic Eruption deals 9d6/15d6/21d6.

Abilities, combat maneuvers, and ancestry gifts all reference this same budget. A Novice class ability that deals damage uses the 2/4/6 line. An Adept Blade maneuver uses 6/9/12. If your homebrew spell or ability doesn't match this table, it's either too weak or too strong. The table is the law. The table is the balance.

See @sec-chapter-arcane-spells and @sec-chapter-divine-spells for the full spell lists. See @sec-chapter-classes for class abilities keyed to this budget.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Worked Example: Building a Fire Mage

Kael wants to burn the world. He's an Arcanist, his class gives him 2 Fire and 1 Energy at creation. His ancestry and culture grant additional Disciplines as well.

**Novice (Firebolt):** Requires 1 Fire. Kael has 2 Fire. He qualifies without even touching his Generals. Firebolt is his immediately.

**Adept (Fireball):** Requires 2 Fire + 1 Energy. Kael has exactly that, 2 Fire, 1 Energy. But the Adept tier requires level 3, so he must wait. Most casters need several levels to reach Adept. Arcanists start closer to the flame and qualify as soon as the gate opens.

**Master (Volcanic Eruption):** Requires 3 Fire + 1 Earth. Kael starts with 2 Fire and 1 Energy, so he needs 1 more Fire and 1 Earth. With level gates in place, Adept unlocks at level 3 and Master at level 7. Kael has time to prepare.

At level 3, Kael takes Fire (now 3 Fire, 1 Energy). At level 6, he takes Earth (now 3 Fire, 1 Earth, 1 Energy). When the Master tier unlocks at level 7, he qualifies for Volcanic Eruption — and any General Disciplines he's earned are still available for other pursuits. He could branch into Protection for defense, Animal for a familiar, or bank them for cross-class talents.

Seven levels to master volcanic fury. Generals got him started. Disciplines got him to Master. No shortcuts. No wildcards. Just the path, walked one step at a time.

That's the Discipline system working as intended. Master spells should be achievable before your campaign's final act, but they should still mean something when you cast them. A level 7 Volcanic Eruption says "I built for this." When Kael calls down the mountain's fury, everyone at the table knows he paid for it.
